definition: Delirium tremens is an acute mental disorder that can happen when a person who has been drinking alcohol chronically suddenly stops or sharply reduces use. It involves confusion, delusions, vivid hallucinations, tremor, agitation, insomnia, and overactivity of the autonomic nervous system such as increased blood pressure, faster heart rate, dilated pupils, and sweating, and it can sometimes be fatal.
